confirmedRules.name: New employee record must pass completeness, ID and salary checks
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Before an employee is created, all four fields (ID, name, department, salary) must be filled in, the ID must be a whole number, and the salary must be a number that is zero or more; name and department are trimmed before saving.
confirmedRules.given: An admin submits the Add Employee form with id='101', name='  Asha ', department='Finance', salary='-500'
confirmedRules.when: The add-employee request is processed
confirmedRules.then: The request is rejected with 'Salary cannot be negative.' and nothing is saved; with salary='15000' the employee is saved as id 101, name 'Asha', department 'Finance', salary 15000.0
confirmedRules.parameters: Minimum salary = 0 (inclusive). ID must parse as a 32-bit integer after trim. Salary parsed as double (any decimals, no rounding). Browser form also sets id min=1 step=1 and salary min=0 step=0.01 (webapp/addEmployee.jsp:20,29) but the server does NOT enforce ID >= 1 or 2-decimal salary.
edgeCases: Blank or whitespace-only field -> 'Please fill in all fields.'
id='10.5' or 'abc' -> 'Employee ID must be a whole number, e.g. 101.'
salary='abc' -> 'Salary must be a number, e.g. 15000.'
salary='0' is accepted
Server accepts id=0 or negative id even though the form requires min=1
salary 'NaN' or 'Infinity' parse successfully in Java and pass the >= 0 check (Infinity) or comparison (NaN < 0 is false) and would be stored
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Server accepts salary='NaN' (NaN < 0 is false) and 'Infinity', and accepts non-positive IDs; only the browser enforces ID >= 1 and cent precision. | The server does not require ID >= 1 (only the browser does). Salary is kept as a binary floating-point value, not a fixed-point currency amount.

confirmedRules.name: Employee ID must be unique
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Each employee has a unique ID chosen by the admin; adding an employee with an ID that already exists is refused.
confirmedRules.given: An employee with ID 101 already exists
confirmedRules.when: An admin tries to add another employee with ID 101
confirmedRules.then: The database rejects the insert (unique violation 23505) and the admin sees 'An employee with this ID already exists. Please choose another ID.'; on success the admin sees 'Employee added successfully!' and returns to Welcome
confirmedRules.parameters: Uniqueness enforced by employee_data.id PRIMARY KEY (schema.sql:11); PostgreSQL SQLSTATE 23505 mapped to the duplicate message. ID is admin-supplied, not generated.
edgeCases: Any other database error -> generic 'Error while adding employee. Please try again.'
Schema uses GENERATED BY DEFAULT identity, so a mix of supplied and generated IDs could collide later

confirmedRules.name: Deleting an employee requires both ID and exact name to match
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: An employee is permanently removed only when the admin supplies both the employee's ID and their exact stored name; otherwise nothing is deleted.
confirmedRules.when: An admin submits Delete with id=101 and name='asha'
confirmedRules.then: No row matches (case- and whitespace-sensitive), nothing is deleted and 'Employee not found!' is intended; with name='Asha' the record is hard-deleted and the session message 'Employee deleted successfully!' is set
confirmedRules.parameters: Match condition: id = ? AND name = ? (exact, case-sensitive, no trimming). Hard delete, no soft-delete/audit.
edgeCases: Missing id or name -> 'Invalid data! Please try again.' (servlet/DeleteEmployeeServlet.java:25,36)
Non-numeric id -> uncaught NumberFormatException (servlet/DeleteEmployeeServlet.java:27)
Names saved on add are trimmed, so a delete with leading/trailing spaces will not match
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: On not-found, DeleteEmployeeServlet writes an alert script and then unconditionally calls sendRedirect('Welcome.jsp') (servlet/DeleteEmployeeServlet.java:31-34), so the 'Employee not found!' alert is likely lost and the user silently lands on Welcome. | On a failed delete, DeleteEmployeeServlet.java:31-34 writes an alert script and then redirects anyway, so the user may never see the 'not found' alert. | When the employee is not found, DeleteEmployeeServlet.java:32-34 writes the 'Employee not found!' script and then calls sendRedirect to Welcome.jsp, so the not-found alert is probably never shown and the admin gets no feedback that nothing was deleted.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Is permanent deletion intended, or should employees move to an inactive/terminated status with retained history, as payroll and HR records retention may require?

confirmedRules.name: Employee operations are not restricted to logged-in admins
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The intended policy is that only a logged-in admin manages employees, but no page or servlet checks the session, so add, edit, delete and list are reachable without logging in, and logout does not end the session.
confirmedRules.given: A user who has never logged in (no adminName in session)
confirmedRules.when: They POST directly to /AddEmployeeServlet, /EditEmployeeServlet, /DeleteEmployeeServlet or GET /ShowEmployeeServlet
confirmedRules.then: The operation executes exactly as for a logged-in admin (including salary changes and deletion)
confirmedRules.parameters: Session attribute 'adminName' is set on login (webapp/Login.jsp:85, servlet/LoginServlet.java:29) and only read for the greeting (webapp/Welcome.jsp:53). No filter, no web.xml security constraint, no session checks in any servlet. Logout is a form posting to index.jsp (webapp/Welcome.jsp:62-64) with no session invalidation.
edgeCases: Welcome.jsp renders for anonymous users with a blank name
After 'Logout', the session still holds adminName
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Missing authorization guard on all employee-data operations; logout does not invalidate the session. | The access check is missing: the app depends on users following the navigation from the login page. | No authorization is enforced on any employee operation, and logout does not invalidate the session (session.invalidate() is never called).
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should every employee operation (add, edit, delete, list) require an authenticated admin session, and should logout invalidate the session? Is there any external control (e.g., reverse-proxy auth) that protects these URLs in production? | Confirm that every employee function (including viewing salaries) must require an authenticated admin session, and whether any admin can see or change any employee's data, or access should be limited by department.

confirmedRules.name: Salary is stored as unrounded floating point
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Salary is held as a binary floating-point number with no currency, rounding or precision rule; whatever decimal the admin enters is stored and shown as Java's raw double text.
confirmedRules.given: An admin adds an employee with salary '15000.005' via a direct request (bypassing the browser's step=0.01)
confirmedRules.when: The employee list is displayed
confirmedRules.then: Salary is stored as DOUBLE PRECISION 15000.005 and displayed via the raw double (e.g. '15000.005'; 15000 shows as '15000.0', large values may show in scientific notation like '1.0E7')
confirmedRules.parameters: Column salary DOUBLE PRECISION NOT NULL; Java type double (model/Employee.java:7); display at webapp/showEmployee.jsp:35 with no formatting; client hint step=0.01 (webapp/addEmployee.jsp:29). No currency, no period (annual/monthly) defined.
edgeCases: Edits store any parsed double, including negatives (see edit rule)
No upper limit on salary
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Money stored as floating point invites rounding error; no currency or pay-period semantics.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: What does salary represent (annual or monthly, which currency), and should it be stored as a fixed-point decimal rounded to 2 places with a defined maximum?

confirmedRules.name: Edit employee: only salary or department can change, and the employee is found by ID alone
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: After an employee is created, only their salary or department can be changed (field names are case-insensitive). Name and ID cannot be changed, and the record is picked by ID only.
confirmedRules.when: An admin submits Edit with id=101, name='Anyone', field='salary', newValue='18000'
confirmedRules.then: Employee 101's salary becomes 18000 and the admin sees 'Employee details updated successfully!'. With field='department', newValue='HR' the department becomes 'HR'. Any other field name, an unknown ID, or a salary that is not a number shows 'Employee not found or invalid data!'
confirmedRules.parameters: Fields that can be edited: 'salary' and 'department' (case-insensitive). The servlet (servlet/EditEmployeeServlet.java:27) requires id, name, field and newValue to be present (not null).
edgeCases: The name the admin enters is required, but it is never compared to the stored name. The update matches on ID only
A negative salary (e.g. -500) is accepted on edit, even though Add rejects it
Department can be set to an empty or whitespace-only value. The form's 'required' check is only in the browser
newValue is not trimmed. A salary of ' 18000' still parses, because Java's Double.parseDouble trims whitespace
A non-numeric ID throws NumberFormatException in the servlet (unhandled, server error page)
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: The rules for add and edit don't match: edit allows a negative salary and ignores the employee name entered as a confirmation, so an admin can edit the wrong employee if they mistype the ID. | Edit skips the 'salary cannot be negative' rule enforced on create, and the required employee name is never used to confirm the target record. | Edit bypasses the add-time salary rule: negative, NaN and Infinity salaries are accepted. The required 'name' field is collected (servlet/EditEmployeeServlet.java:23,27) but never used to confirm the employee identity, unlike delete which requires id+name match.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should an edit require the entered name to match the employee's name (as Delete does), and should a salary of zero or more be enforced on edit as well as on add? | Should salary edits apply the same non-negative (and any range) rules as creation, and should the employee name be checked to confirm the record being updated, as delete does?

confirmedRules.name: Open admin self-registration with a unique numeric admin ID
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Anyone can register as an admin by choosing a whole-number admin ID that is not already taken and a name; no approval or invitation is needed.
confirmedRules.when: A visitor submits Sign Up with id=5, name=' Ravi '
confirmedRules.then: Admin 5 'Ravi' is created and the visitor sees 'Sign up successful! Please log in.'. id='abc' gives 'Admin ID must be a whole number'. If ID 5 already exists, the visitor sees 'An admin with this ID already exists. Please choose another ID.' (SQLSTATE 23505)
confirmedRules.parameters: Uniqueness comes from the PRIMARY KEY on admin_data.id (schema.sql:6). The form (webapp/signup.jsp:56) sets min=1 in the browser only.
edgeCases: The server does not require a name. A missing or empty name is stored as null or '', and that admin can then log in with an empty name only if the browser allows it
An ID of 0 or a negative ID is accepted by the server
There is no approval workflow, invitation code or role level. Every registrant is a full admin
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: An admin name is not required on the server, and there is no check on who may register as an admin. | Open self-registration with no approval or invitation means any unauthenticated visitor can give themselves full admin rights over employee and salary data. | Unrestricted admin creation plus name-only login means any visitor can obtain full employee-management rights; server accepts empty/null admin names and IDs <= 0.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Is open self-registration as an admin intended, or should new admins need approval or an invitation from an existing admin?

confirmedRules.name: Logout does not end the admin session
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Clicking Logout only goes back to the home page; the admin's session (adminName) stays active.
confirmedRules.when: They click Logout
confirmedRules.then: They are taken to index.jsp, but the session is not invalidated. Going back to Welcome.jsp still shows 'Welcome, Arun!' until the server session times out
confirmedRules.parameters: Logout = a form posting to index.jsp. index.jsp (webapp/index.jsp:74-83) has no session code. The session timeout is the container default (not configured).
edgeCases: On a shared computer, the next user inherits the previous admin's session
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Logout should invalidate the session.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: What session timeout and logout behaviour does the business require for admin sessions?

confirmedRules.name: Admin login by matching ID and name (no password)
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: An admin is logged in when the Admin ID and Admin Name they enter exactly match a stored admin record; no password is involved.
confirmedRules.when: A user submits Login.jsp with id=101 and name="Priya"
confirmedRules.then: The session attribute adminName is set to "Priya" and the user is redirected to Welcome.jsp; with name="priya" or id=102 the message 'Invalid ID or Name. Please try again.' is shown
confirmedRules.parameters: Match query: SELECT 1 FROM admin_data WHERE id = ? AND name = ? (dao/AdminDAO.java:31-44), exact case-sensitive name match; credential factors = ID + name only
edgeCases: Name is not trimmed during login while it was trimmed at sign-up, so ' Priya' fails
Non-numeric ID -> same generic invalid message
A duplicate path exists in servlet/LoginServlet.java:21-34 (same rule; throws instead of showing a message on a non-numeric ID; the form posts to Login.jsp, not to LoginServlet)
Database error is treated as a failed login (AdminDAO returns false)
No lockout or limit on attempts
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Authentication uses only an ID and a display name, both guessable, with no password or attempt limit. | Authentication relies solely on ID + name with no password or attempt limiting; names are easily guessable. Two divergent login implementations exist (Login.jsp scriptlet and LoginServlet). | No secret is checked, so the admin name works like a guessable password. Combined with open sign-up (see the sign-up rule), anyone can get admin access.

confirmedRules.name: New employee record validation and creation
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A new employee needs an ID, name, department, and salary, all non-blank. The ID must be a whole number, the salary must be a number that is not negative, and the ID must not already be in use.
confirmedRules.when: An admin submits id=205, name=' Ravi ', department='Finance', salary='15000.50'
confirmedRules.then: An employee_data row (205, 'Ravi', 'Finance', 15000.50) is stored with text trimmed, and the alert 'Employee added successfully!' sends the user to Welcome.jsp
confirmedRules.parameters: Minimum salary = 0 (inclusive); duplicate-ID SQLSTATE = 23505; salary stored as DOUBLE PRECISION NOT NULL (schema.sql:10-15); client form hints id min=1, salary min=0 step=0.01 (addEmployee.jsp:20,29)
edgeCases: Any blank field -> 'Please fill in all fields.'
id='10.5' or 'abc' -> 'Employee ID must be a whole number'
salary='abc' -> 'Salary must be a number'
salary=-1 -> 'Salary cannot be negative.'; salary=0 is accepted
Duplicate ID -> 'An employee with this ID already exists'
Server does not enforce ID >= 1 or 2-decimal salary precision; 'NaN' or 'Infinity' parse as valid doubles and pass the negative check
Salary is stored as floating point, not exact currency
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Salary is stored as a binary floating-point number (DOUBLE) and is not rounded to cents. Values like NaN or Infinity pass validation.

confirmedRules.name: Employee listing shows all records unfiltered
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The employee list shows every employee's ID, name, department, and salary, with no filtering, paging, or guaranteed order.
confirmedRules.when: Someone opens ShowEmployeeServlet
confirmedRules.then: All three rows are listed with raw salary values (e.g. 15000.5), in database order
confirmedRules.parameters: Query: SELECT id, name, department, salary FROM employee_data (no ORDER BY, no WHERE); rendered in webapp/showEmployee.jsp:26-40
edgeCases: A database error returns null, which renders as an empty table
Salary is shown with Java double formatting, not currency formatting
Values are written without HTML escaping
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should the employee list be sorted (e.g. by ID or name), and should salary visibility be limited to certain roles?
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: No ORDER BY, so ordering is undefined; DB errors are silently shown as an empty list.

confirmedRules.name: Failed delete still sends the user to the home page as if it worked
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: After a delete attempt, the user is always redirected to the Welcome page, even when no employee matched. The 'Employee not found!' alert is written to the response before the redirect, so it is effectively lost.
confirmedRules.given: No employee has ID 999 with name 'Bob'
confirmedRules.when: An admin submits the delete form with id=999 and name=Bob
confirmedRules.then: Nothing is deleted, the 'not found' alert script is written, and then sendRedirect('Welcome.jsp') runs anyway (line 34). The user usually lands on Welcome without any error shown. On success, 'Employee deleted successfully!' is stored in the session.
confirmedRules.parameters: Session attribute key 'message' (line 30). Redirect target: Welcome.jsp. Failure target in the alert: deleteEmployee.jsp.
edgeCases: A non-numeric ID throws an uncaught NumberFormatException (line 27), which shows as an HTTP 500
A blank name passes the null check and simply matches nothing
The success message is put in the session, but no JSP ever reads the 'message' attribute, so users never see success confirmations for edit or delete either
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: The redirect at line 34 sits outside the if/else, so a failed deletion looks like a success to the user. If the response is already committed, sendRedirect may also throw an IllegalStateException. | On failure the servlet writes an alert and then calls sendRedirect anyway (line 34 runs on both branches), so the failure message is lost. | sendRedirect at line 34 runs on the failure path too. The response has no return/else, so the failure alert is lost or the request errors.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: When a deletion matches no employee, should the user stay on the delete page with a clear 'not found' error? | Should a failed delete (no ID+name match) send the user back to the delete form with an error, or to the Welcome page?

confirmedRules.name: Unused employee self-login check (ID plus name)
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: There is a check that would treat an employee as authenticated when an employee_data row matches both the ID and the exact name. No servlet or JSP calls it, so employee self-service login does not exist today.
confirmedRules.when: validateEmployee(101, 'Ravi') is called
confirmedRules.then: It returns true. validateEmployee(101, 'ravi') returns false because the match is case-sensitive. Any database error returns false.
confirmedRules.parameters: Lookup: SELECT 1 FROM employee_data WHERE id=? AND name=?. Similar dead code: AdminDAO.getAdminById (AdminDAO.java:47-65) is also never called.
edgeCases: Duplicate names under different IDs do not matter because the ID is the primary key
A database failure returns false (not authenticated) instead of an error
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Was employee self-service login (by ID and name) ever a requirement, or is this leftover code that can be dropped in the rewrite? | Was employee self-service login ever a requirement, or can validateEmployee be dropped?
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Dead code. The comment claims 'employee login', but no executable path exercises it.

confirmedRules.name: Record IDs are typed in by users even though the database can generate them
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Both the admin and employee tables define the ID as an auto-generated identity ('GENERATED BY DEFAULT'). The application always supplies the ID the user typed, so the generated sequence is never used or advanced. Admin name and employee name and department may be NULL at the database level.
confirmedRules.given: The admin_data identity sequence is at 1 and users have created admins with IDs 1 and 2
confirmedRules.when: Any future insert omits the ID (for example a data migration or a new feature)
confirmedRules.then: The database generates id=1, which collides with an existing row and fails with a unique violation (SQLState 23505)
confirmedRules.parameters: admin_data.id and employee_data.id: INT GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY. name, department and admin name are VARCHAR(255) and nullable. salary is DOUBLE PRECISION NOT NULL. Client-side ID minimum is 1 (addEmployee.jsp:20, signup.jsp:56, Login.jsp:68).
edgeCases: Names longer than 255 characters are rejected by the database, which surfaces as a generic error
The INT range caps IDs at 2,147,483,647, and larger values fail Integer.parseInt
The ID minimum of 1 is only enforced in the browser. ID 0 or negative IDs can be posted directly unless the server checks them
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should employee and admin IDs be assigned by the business (manually) or generated by the system, and should name and department be mandatory at the database level? | Are employee and admin IDs meant to be chosen by users (for example an HR payroll number), or should the system assign them? | Should employee and admin IDs be business-assigned (for example a payroll number) or system-generated?
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Mixing user-supplied IDs with identity columns leaves the sequences out of step with the data.

confirmedRules.name: Salary shown in the employee list as a raw unformatted number
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The employee list prints each salary using Java's default double-to-text conversion, with no currency symbol, no fixed two decimals and no rounding.
confirmedRules.when: An admin opens 'Show List of Employees'
confirmedRules.then: The salaries appear as '50000.0', '1234.5' and '1.2E7' (scientific notation from 10,000,000 upward)
confirmedRules.parameters: No locale, currency or decimal format is applied. Values come from emp.getSalary() via the <%= %> expression.
edgeCases: When the DAO returns null on a database error, the table is shown empty with no error message (lines 27-28)
Values that cannot be represented exactly, such as 0.1 + 0.2 accumulations, may display as 0.30000000000000004
Name and department are printed without HTML escaping
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: What salary display format is expected (currency, 2 decimals, thousands separators)?

confirmedRules.name: Edit employee request guard: four fields required, but the supplied name is never verified
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: An edit request must include employee ID, employee name, the field to change and a new value, but the name is only checked for presence and is never compared with the stored employee, so knowing the ID is enough to change a record.
confirmedRules.when: An edit is submitted with id=101, name='Bob', field='department', newValue='Finance'
confirmedRules.then: Alice's department becomes 'Finance' and 'Employee details updated successfully!' is shown. If any of the four parameters is missing, 'Invalid data! Please try again.' is shown. If the update matches no row or the field is not salary/department, 'Employee not found or invalid data!' is shown.
confirmedRules.parameters: Required parameters: id, name, field, newValue (only a null check, so empty strings pass). The form offers field values 'department' and 'salary' (webapp/editEmployee.jsp:25-29). The ID input is a free-text box with no numeric constraint (editEmployee.jsp:20).
edgeCases: A non-numeric ID such as 'abc' reaches Integer.parseInt without a try/catch (servlet line 29), so the user gets an HTTP 500 error instead of the 'invalid data' alert
An empty newValue '' passes the null check; with field=department the department is set to an empty string
The delete flow requires ID and name to match, but edit does not, so the two operations apply different identity checks
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: The edit form and servlet ask for the employee name, which suggests it was meant as a second identity check like delete, but the name is never passed to the DAO. Non-numeric IDs are not caught.

confirmedRules.name: Second admin login endpoint with weaker input handling (LoginServlet)
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A second login endpoint exists that also accepts an admin ID and name and starts an admin session when they match. Unlike the page-based login, it does not trim the ID or handle a non-numeric ID. No page in the app currently posts to it, but it can still be called directly.
confirmedRules.when: A POST to /LoginServlet sends id=101, name='Root'
confirmedRules.then: Session attribute adminName='Root' is set and the user is redirected to Welcome.jsp. A wrong pair shows 'Incorrect name or id' and returns to Login.jsp. id=' 101' or 'abc' causes an unhandled error (HTTP 500).
confirmedRules.parameters: Same credential rule as Login.jsp: ID plus exact name, no password (dao/AdminDAO.java:31-44). Login.jsp posts to itself (webapp/Login.jsp:66), not to LoginServlet.
edgeCases: A missing id parameter causes a NumberFormatException on null
Login.jsp trims the ID (Login.jsp:84) but LoginServlet does not, so the two paths accept different inputs
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Is /LoginServlet still an intended entry point, or should it be removed so that only one login rule exists? | Is /LoginServlet still used by any external client, or can it be retired in favour of the Login.jsp flow? | Is /LoginServlet still meant to be used (for example by another client), or can it be removed in favor of a single login flow?
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: There are two inconsistent implementations of the same authentication rule, and the unused one is still exposed. | Duplicate authentication path with different validation behaviour. Only one should survive the rewrite. | This duplicate authentication path is reachable even though no page links to it, and its edge-case behavior differs from Login.jsp. A rewrite should have exactly one login rule.

confirmedRules.name: Admin name must match exactly as stored, and blank names are allowed at sign-up
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Sign-up trims the admin name before saving it but does not require a name and only checks that the ID is a whole number. Login compares the name exactly as typed, without trimming and case-sensitively, so some sign-ups cannot log in.
confirmedRules.given: An admin signs up with id=101 and name 'Root ' (trailing space)
confirmedRules.when: They log in with id=101 and name 'Root '
confirmedRules.then: The stored name is 'Root', the comparison against 'Root ' fails, and login is refused. Logging in as 'Root' succeeds and 'root' fails.
confirmedRules.parameters: No minimum or maximum ID on the server; the browser form requires min=1, step=1 (webapp/signup.jsp:56). Name column is VARCHAR(255) and nullable (schema.sql:5-8).
edgeCases: A direct POST with no name stores a NULL name, and that admin can never log in because SQL 'name = ?' never matches NULL
A direct POST with a blank name stores '' as the name
IDs of 0 or below are accepted by the server even though the form requires at least 1
An ID-taken conflict (SQLState 23505) shows 'An admin with this ID already exists'
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Names are trimmed on write but not on login comparison, and blank or missing names are accepted.

confirmedRules.name: Employee and admin IDs: browser requires a positive whole number, server accepts any integer
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The Add Employee form allows only IDs of 1 or more and salaries of 0 or more with up to 2 decimal places, but the server enforces only 'whole number' for the ID and 'not negative' for the salary, so a direct request can create ID 0, negative IDs, or salaries with more than 2 decimals.
confirmedRules.given: A client posts directly to AddEmployeeServlet
confirmedRules.when: It sends id=-5, salary=1000.123
confirmedRules.then: The employee is created with ID -5 and salary 1000.123. Through the form, the browser would reject both values.
confirmedRules.parameters: Client-side: ID min=1, step=1; salary min=0, step=0.01 (addEmployee.jsp:20,29). Server-side: Integer.parseInt for the ID; salary must parse and be >= 0 (AddEmployeeServlet.java:34-52).
edgeCases: The edit and delete forms use free-text ID inputs with no client constraint
The 2-decimal salary precision implied by step=0.01 is never applied on the server
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Range and precision rules exist only in the browser.

confirmedRules.name: Unused employee identity check (validateEmployee) and admin lookup (getAdminById)
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The code contains a check that an employee exists with a given ID and exact name, labelled 'Validate employee login', which suggests a planned employee self-service login. It is never called, and neither is the admin lookup by ID (dao/AdminDAO.java:46-65).
confirmedRules.when: validateEmployee(101, 'Alice Smith') is called
confirmedRules.then: It returns true. Any mismatch or database error returns false. No servlet or JSP calls it.
confirmedRules.parameters: Match rule: id = ? AND name = ? (exact, case-sensitive).
edgeCases: A DB error is treated as 'not valid' rather than surfaced
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Was employee self-service login (by employee ID and name) ever a requirement, and should the new system carry it over or drop it?

confirmedRules.name: Employee list shows an empty table when the employee data cannot be read
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: If loading the employee list fails, the DAO returns no list and the page shows an empty table with headers, so a database outage looks the same as having no employees.
confirmedRules.when: An admin opens Show List of Employees (ShowEmployeeServlet, servlet/ShowEmployeeServlet.java:23-30)
confirmedRules.then: An empty table with ID/Name/Department/Salary headers is shown and no error message appears
confirmedRules.parameters: Salary is shown as the raw double (for example 50000.0 or 1.0E7) with no currency formatting or rounding.
edgeCases: Large salaries display in scientific notation (for example 1.0E7)
NaN or negative salaries saved through edit display as-is
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: A failed load cannot be told apart from an empty workforce.

confirmedRules.name: Salary edits skip the non-negative and format checks that apply when an employee is added
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: When salary is changed, the only checks are that all four form fields are present and that the new value parses as a number. Negative, NaN and Infinity values are all accepted, even though adding an employee requires a non-negative salary.
confirmedRules.when: An admin submits the Edit form with id=101, field=salary, newValue=-5000
confirmedRules.then: The salary is updated to -5000.0 and the user sees 'Employee details updated successfully!' (stored in the session). A value such as 'NaN' or 'Infinity' is also saved.
confirmedRules.parameters: Required params: id, name, field, newValue (null check only, so an empty string passes); allowed field values 'salary' or 'department' (case-insensitive, EmployeeDAO.java:42-45); salary parsed with Double.parseDouble (EmployeeDAO.java:44)
edgeCases: Empty newValue for department sets department to an empty string
Non-numeric id (the form field is type=text, editEmployee.jsp:20) throws an unhandled NumberFormatException at line 29 and returns an HTTP 500, not the 'Invalid data' alert
Non-numeric salary is caught in the DAO and reported as 'Employee not found or invalid data!'
Name is required by the form, but the servlet never passes it to the DAO, so it is not checked
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Salary validation on edit does not match the add rule, so an edit can store a negative or non-finite salary. | Salary integrity rules differ between add and edit. Negative, NaN and Infinity salaries can be stored through edit, and NaN can be stored through add. | Salary changes can produce negative, NaN or Infinity salaries even though the add path forbids negative salaries. The edit form also asks for the employee's name but never checks it, so the admin may think the name is being verified when it is not.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should salary edits follow the same rules as new employees (non-negative, at most 2 decimals), and should the employee name entered on the edit form have to match the stored name?

confirmedRules.name: Success confirmations are stored but never shown
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Edit and delete store a success message in the session, but the Welcome page never reads or clears it, so the confirmations are invisible and stay in the session.
confirmedRules.given: An admin has just edited employee 101
confirmedRules.when: The browser is redirected to Welcome.jsp
confirmedRules.then: Only 'Welcome, <adminName>!' and the action buttons appear. The session attribute 'message' = 'Employee details updated successfully!' is not shown and is not removed.
confirmedRules.parameters: Session attribute key 'message' (set at EditEmployeeServlet.java:33 and DeleteEmployeeServlet.java:30)
edgeCases: A message left in the session could be shown later if a future page starts displaying 'message'
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Dead confirmation side effect: users get no confirmation that a change was saved.

confirmedRules.name: Admin accounts have a create-only lifecycle
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Admins can only be created (sign-up) and looked up. There is no way to deactivate, rename or delete an admin, and admins have no status field.
confirmedRules.given: Admin id=7 'Carol' has left the organisation
confirmedRules.when: Someone tries to revoke her access
confirmedRules.then: The application has no operation for it, so the admin row stays valid forever and 'Carol' can still log in with id 7 and her name.
confirmedRules.parameters: admin_data columns: id, name only (schema.sql:5-8); operations: saveAdmin (INSERT), validateAdmin, getAdminById (never called by any page or servlet)
edgeCases: getAdminById is dead code
Nothing enforces unique admin names, so two admins can share a name with different IDs
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: There is no way to revoke admin access through the application.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Does the business need to disable or remove admin accounts, and should admins have an active/inactive status?

confirmedRules.name: Department is free text with no reference list
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Department is any text the admin types, both on add and on edit. It is not checked against a list of valid departments, so spelling variants become different departments.
confirmedRules.when: An admin edits field=department, newValue='sales '
confirmedRules.then: The department is saved as 'sales ' (case and trailing space kept) and is treated as different from 'Sales'.
confirmedRules.parameters: Field selector options: department (default selection), salary; newValue is a type=text required input; add form department field at addEmployee.jsp:25-26
edgeCases: The edit field defaults to Department, so a salary typed without changing the selector is saved as the department text
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Is there a canonical department list that values should be validated against?
